title: An idempotent endomorphism splits its object into the kernel and the kernel of its complement
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file homology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that when an idempotent endomorphism and its complement each have at least one of a kernel or a cokernel, all four exist and the object splits as a direct sum of any choice of one kernel or cokernel of the idempotent and one kernel or cokernel of its complement, with the structure given by the four constructed morphisms (statement lines 638-656). The proof is a complete argument: the two splitting identities are read off from the lemma on the kernel and cokernel of an idempotent (proof lines 658-661), and the construction makes the sum of the two composites equal to the identity, so the four morphisms satisfy the characterizing identities of a direct sum and the displayed isomorphisms follow (proof lines 662-663). The non-formal content is the verification of the identities of a direct sum. The claim is H2: a structured input with each input named.
